purpose: Individually authored episode questions and coverage boundaries for Home & Lifestyle. The subject progression is organized by concrete content rather than a topic-by-angle multiplication.

topics.question: How can a household identify which rooms are failing its daily routines?
topics.coverage: Map waking, cooking, work, care and rest through a consented day-in-the-life exercise; distinguish residents' priorities from an aspirational room photograph.

topics.question: What changes when a small room must support several activities?
topics.coverage: Compare storage, circulation, furniture movement and transitions in one measured layout; keep structural alterations outside the proposed makeover.

topics.question: How can shared homes negotiate clutter without imposing one person's standard?
topics.coverage: Document different definitions of useful possessions, shared zones and decision authority; use consented examples rather than diagnosing occupants from their belongings.

topics.question: Why can a visually tidy space still be difficult to use?
topics.coverage: Trace access height, retrieval effort, labels and return paths for everyday objects; include disability and household variation rather than only decorative symmetry.

topics.question: How should a cleaning method be matched to the surface rather than a viral tip?
topics.coverage: Consult manufacturer care guidance for wood, stone, textiles and coatings; compare compatibility and test-area limits without inventing chemical mixtures.

topics.question: What is the difference between cleaning a surface and making a disinfection claim?
topics.coverage: Compare intended purpose, product labeling, contact conditions and evidence requirements from official guidance; exclude homemade formulations and universal germ-killing promises.

topics.question: How can a realistic cleaning routine prioritize limited time and energy?
topics.coverage: Separate high-use zones, access needs, household roles and maintenance frequency; use an illustrative routine without implying a clinical cleanliness standard.

topics.question: Why can laundry results depend on more than the detergent chosen?
topics.coverage: Examine fabric labels, load size, water conditions, temperature and drying; verify appliance instructions and avoid unqualified stain-removal recipes.

categories.title: Kitchen, food storage and domestic work

topics.question: How does a kitchen workflow change for one cook versus several cooks?
topics.coverage: Follow preparation, cooking, serving and cleanup in a measured existing kitchen; include shared access and exclude electrical or plumbing modification advice.

topics.question: What makes a household food inventory useful without creating extra waste?
topics.coverage: Compare visibility, date labeling, meal planning and realistic purchase quantities; refer any storage-duration claims to current food-safety authorities.

topics.question: How can meal preparation account for shift work and irregular schedules?
topics.coverage: Map available time, equipment, storage and household preferences; distinguish organizational strategies from individualized dietary or medical recommendations.

topics.question: Why is the hidden planning behind domestic work difficult to divide fairly?
topics.coverage: Separate noticing, scheduling, purchasing and execution through consented household accounts; avoid assuming equality from the number of visible chores alone.

categories.reading_subcategory: Kitchen, food storage and domestic work

topics.question: How can lighting be arranged around tasks in a rented room?
topics.coverage: Compare glare, shadows, fixture positions and permitted portable options; use product instructions and keep rewiring outside the episode.

topics.question: What can soft furnishings change about room sound and what can they not change?
topics.coverage: Separate reverberation, sound transmission and source noise with a bounded measurement example; avoid representing decorative panels as proven structural soundproofing.

topics.question: How should a home-comfort complaint be documented before buying a device?
topics.coverage: Record room use, temperature, humidity and timing with stated sensor limits; distinguish comfort observations from diagnosing damp, mold or building defects.

topics.question: How can a first-home essentials list separate immediate needs from optional upgrades?
topics.coverage: Build a transparent illustrative budget around sleeping, cooking, hygiene and access; include recurring costs without using undated shopping recommendations.

topics.question: What should be compared when renting, buying or borrowing an infrequently used household item?
topics.coverage: Calculate storage, maintenance, fees and frequency for one item; label assumptions and avoid treating convenience as identical for every household.

topics.question: How can a move be planned around fragile items, records and service continuity?
topics.coverage: Trace inventory, labeling, access windows and handover responsibilities; require dated local operator terms for costs and avoid exposing private addresses.

topics.question: What does the total cost of a home appliance include beyond purchase price?
topics.coverage: Compare energy, consumables, service, useful life and financing under explicit assumptions; defer current tariffs and model claims to official documentation.

topics.question: How can storage be adapted for a resident with changing mobility?
topics.coverage: Begin with consented reach and movement preferences, stable placement and access paths; refer structural or clinical adaptations to qualified assessment.

topics.question: What changes when a home must accommodate guests and ongoing care work?
topics.coverage: Examine privacy, resting space, bathroom access and caregiver routines; avoid inferring a family's needs from age or diagnosis alone.

topics.question: How can a sensory-friendly room be evaluated by its actual occupant?
topics.coverage: Document lighting, textures, noise and control preferences through consented feedback; distinguish individual comfort from treatment claims.

topics.question: How can a renter distinguish routine upkeep from a repair to report?
topics.coverage: Use a named jurisdiction's tenancy guidance and a documented responsibility checklist; keep fault diagnosis and legal conclusions separate from reporting observations.

topics.question: What belongs in a household emergency plan for a specific local hazard?
topics.coverage: Use current local emergency-management instructions to cover contacts, access needs and supplies; exclude generalized survival promises and unverified hazard forecasts.

topics.question: How can households track maintenance without collecting unnecessary personal data?
topics.coverage: Compare a paper log with a private digital record for warranties, service and recurring checks; use fictitious identifiers and define retention boundaries.

topics.question: What should happen to unwanted household goods before they become mixed waste?
topics.coverage: Trace repair, donation acceptance, reuse and authorized disposal requirements locally; do not assume charities accept every item or every material is recyclable.

topics.question: How do staged home images alter perceptions of ordinary domestic life?
topics.coverage: Compare crop, lighting, absent possessions and sponsorship with permission-cleared examples; distinguish aesthetic choices from evidence about residents' actual routines.

topics.question: Can a low-buy household experiment measure useful change without becoming a moral scorecard?
topics.coverage: Define a voluntary baseline, spending categories, repair attempts and reported tradeoffs; avoid equating reduced purchasing with universal wellbeing or virtue.

topics.question: How can a home makeover be documented honestly when only a small budget is available?
topics.coverage: Show retained items, labor, borrowed tools and full costs through an original room example; disclose gifted products and exclude unsafe modifications.

topics.question: How can a household inventory reduce duplicate buying without becoming another chore?
topics.coverage: Compare update effort, shared access, useful categories and exceptions with a small practical example.

topics.question: Why can a room feel uncomfortable even when the thermostat shows a familiar temperature?
topics.coverage: Compare drafts, radiant surfaces, humidity, activity and personal preferences without diagnosing a building.

topics.question: What does a home maintenance plan need when residents rent rather than own?
topics.coverage: Separate reporting, permissions, landlord responsibility, documentation and qualified work for one jurisdiction.

topics.question: How can a shared home distribute tasks that have different standards of done?
topics.coverage: Define outcomes, timing, responsibility and renegotiation using fictional household examples.

topics.question: How can a household compare energy used by two activities when appliance ratings and time spent differ?
topics.coverage: Use hypothetical power, cycles, standby use and service delivered; distinguish a label rating from measured household consumption and avoid invented savings.

topics.question: What information changes a household decision to repair an appliance rather than replace it?
topics.coverage: Compare fault diagnosis by a qualified person, parts, support, downtime, remaining service and lifecycle assumptions; exclude repair procedures, electrical testing or a universal buy-new rule.

topics.question: When does the kitchen work triangle help or hinder a real household?
topics.coverage: Test the historical sink-stove-fridge rule against a named kitchen and its actual users; BANK-064-021 retains the general multi-cook workflow question.

topics.question: What changes when a household tries the KonMari category-first method?
topics.coverage: Document a bounded before-and-after routine, storage and discard decisions; do not promise permanent freedom from clutter.

topics.question: How does Swedish death cleaning differ from an ordinary seasonal clear-out?
topics.coverage: Trace the published method and a voluntary household example; avoid age quotas, mortality pressure or guaranteed emotional outcomes.

topics.question: How can a micro-apartment be evaluated for daily life beyond its floor area?
topics.coverage: Use a named small unit to test storage, daylight, privacy and code constraints; avoid universal luxury claims from an area figure.

topics.question: Can a one-minute tidying rule change a household’s actual cleaning workload?
topics.coverage: Test the habit over a bounded period and include tasks longer than a minute; distinguish routine adherence from cleanliness or fairness outcomes.

topics.question: How should a household compare warm and cool light for a particular room?
topics.coverage: Compare illuminance, color temperature, timing and occupant preference; do not diagnose mood or sleep from a Kelvin number alone.

topics.question: Why does acoustic foam change room echo more than sound through a wall?
topics.coverage: Distinguish absorption inside a room from isolation between rooms with a defined test; BANK-064-026 covers ordinary soft furnishings.

topics.question: When can a courtyard or cross-breeze improve comfort without mechanical cooling?
topics.coverage: Compare orientation, climate, openings and night conditions for a documented home; do not claim passive cooling always replaces AC.

topics.question: How do low-e window choices change heat gain and heat loss?
topics.coverage: Use U-factor, solar heat-gain coefficient and orientation for a climate-specific comparison; avoid a universal “traps winter heat, blocks summer heat” promise.

topics.question: When does home battery storage change a solar household’s electricity bill?
topics.coverage: Compare tariff, load timing, battery losses and backup value in an explicit scenario; do not claim it automatically beats the utility.

topics.question: When does cross-laminated timber make sense in a home project?
topics.coverage: Compare structural system, fire design, moisture handling and embodied-carbon boundaries in a documented building; avoid saying CLT simply replaces all steel or concrete.

topics.question: Which Earthship features perform as claimed in a documented climate?
topics.coverage: Compare tire-wall construction, thermal comfort, water and maintenance records for one occupied dwelling; separate experimental aims from proven autonomy.

topics.question: What must be maintained for a home to run energy, water and robots as linked systems?
topics.coverage: Map current components, failure modes, service labor and resource balances; keep 2040 autonomy as a scenario, not an operational fact.

categories.title: Health, water and savings claim boundaries

topics.question: Which indoor activities create measurable air-quality concerns at home?
topics.coverage: Compare source, ventilation and measurement for cooking, cleaning or furnishings; avoid treating every sealed home as toxic or offering medical diagnosis.

topics.question: What can limewash and mineral paints change about a damp wall?
topics.coverage: Separate vapor permeability from fixing leaks, condensation and existing mold; reject the claim that any paint prevents mold forever.

topics.question: What must a household check before using greywater for irrigation?
topics.coverage: Separate source water, local rules, soil and plant exposure for a stated location; avoid prescriptive plumbing or health advice.

topics.question: What does evidence actually show about plants and cognitive performance indoors?
topics.coverage: Separate biophilic design claims from controlled outcome measures, light, maintenance and preference; do not repeat the archived 15% claim as fact.

topics.question: What evidence is needed before roof-collected rainwater is used for drinking?
topics.coverage: Distinguish collection, storage, treatment, testing and local regulation; do not provide an unverified filter recipe or potable-water guarantee.

topics.question: How can a smart thermostat’s savings claim be tested in one home?
topics.coverage: Compare baseline, weather, occupancy and tariff before crediting learning algorithms; reject a universal 15% bill reduction.

topics.question: When can shifting cooling time reduce electricity cost without worsening comfort?
topics.coverage: Use a stated tariff, thermal mass, weather and occupant schedule; do not promise a 30% AC-bill cut.

topics.question: What should a household document when it suspects indoor mold?
topics.coverage: Focus on moisture source, visible extent and appropriate professional assessment; do not diagnose brain injury or equate every dark patch with a species.

topics.question: How should a low-flow showerhead’s savings and performance be checked?
topics.coverage: Compare measured flow, use time, water rate and spray tests; avoid a fixed price, half-bill promise or pressure guarantee.

# Home & Lifestyle Channel Master Topic Roadmap (Scratch to Advanced)
**Niche:** 064 Home & Lifestyle (Home_Living)  
**Channel Language:** English (YouTube)  
**Target Audience:** Homeowners, Interior Designers, Organization Buffs, DIY Renovators, Healthy Living Seekers (Global)  
**Production Format:** 10-Minute Documentary Explainer Episodes (600s, 75 Fixed 8s Scenes)  
**Execution & Sync Report:** [topics/064_home_lifestyle/TOPICS_COVERED_REPORT.md](./TOPICS_COVERED_REPORT.md)  

---

## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Home & Lifestyle across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Spatial Ergonomics, Lighting Psychology & Decluttering Systems (Scratch / Beginner)** — Circadian rhythm Kelvin lighting color temperatures, the KonMari category sorting system, corridor traffic flow clearance, and VOC indoor air toxins.
- **Tier 2: Smart Home Mesh, Passive Thermal Design & Soundproofing (Intermediate)** — Zigbee/Thread mesh networks, cross-ventilation passive airflow, double-pane Low-E window coatings, and acoustic mass-loaded vinyl decoupling.
- **Tier 3: Heat Pumps, Home Battery Storage & Non-Toxic Materials (Upper Intermediate)** — Heat pump coefficient of performance (COP) thermodynamics, home solar battery time-of-use peak shaving, lime wash mineral paints, and greywater recycling.
- **Tier 4: Prefab Modular Living, Biophilic Architecture & Off-Grid Autonomy (Advanced / Expert)** — Cross-laminated timber prefab construction, living indoor moss particulate air scrubbers, off-grid rainwater micro-filtration engineering, and hyper-compact micro-apartments.

---

## 2. Topic Styles & Narrative Angles (32 Curated Formats)

Every episode is produced using one of the 32 niche angle presets defined in [`REGISTRY/Niches/064_home_lifestyle/ANGLE_PLAN.json`](file:///h:/script-raw-/REGISTRY/Niches/064_home_lifestyle/ANGLE_PLAN.json):
